name: Shemeber
overview: Shemeber was a male figure known as the King of Zeboiim, a city mentioned in the book of Genesis. Beyond his royal title, Scripture does not provide additional personal or tribal details. His brief mention situates him within the context of ancient Near Eastern monarchies.
namesAndTitles: The name Shemeber appears simply as a proper name with no specific meaning provided in the biblical text. His title, King of Zeboiim, identifies his rulership over the city of Zeboiim, indicating his political authority during the time recorded in Genesis 14:2.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Shemeber beyond his designation as king. No additional familial connections or descendants are mentioned in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Shemeber's significance lies in his role as one of the kings allied during the events described in Genesis 14:2. His mention highlights the political landscape and the presence of multiple city-states governed by kings in the patriarchal period. Although details about his actions are limited, his inclusion underscores the historical reality of regional monarchies encountered by the patriarchs.
